new: Service of documents on respondents in prison (1) This section applies to an adult respondent who is a prisoner held in a prison. (2) A document that is required to be served under this Act on the respondent may be served by leaving it with the Governor of the prison if— (a) the person serving the document, or another person on their behalf, confirms that the respondent will be present at the prison for a visit at a specified time; and (b) the respondent has been advised before the visit that the purpose of the visit is to serve the respondent with a document under this Act; and (c) the respondent— (i) refuses to accept the visit; or (ii) accepts the visit but refuses to accept service of the documents during the visit. (3) For the purposes of this Act, the document is taken to have been personally served on the respondent when it is left with the Governor of the prison. (4) The Governor must deliver the document, or cause it to be delivered, to the respondent as soon as reasonably practicable after it has been left with the Governor. 202BB Prisoner released from custody before document can be delivered (1) If the respondent ceases to be a prisoner before the Governor of the prison can deliver or cause to be delivered to the respondent a document left under section 202BA, the Governor must as soon as possible— (a) notify the Chief Commissioner of Police that the document was not delivered to the respondent before the respondent ceased to be a prisoner; and (b) give to the Chief Commissioner of Police a true copy of the document. (2) The Chief Commissioner of Police must deliver the document, or cause it to be delivered, to the respondent as soon as reasonably practicable after it has been given to the Chief Commissioner of Police. 202BC Governor of prison may delegate function The Governor of a prison, by instrument, may delegate any function under section 202BA or 202BB to an officer or class of officer within the meaning of section 14 of the Corrections Act 1986.

new: Continuing protection of former child protected person (1) This section applies to an application for variation or revocation of a family violence intervention order if— (a) more than one adult is a protected person for the order; and (b) at least one but not all of the adult protected persons is a former child protected person. (2) If the court is satisfied that there has been a change in the need to protect the former child protected person from being subjected to family violence committed by the respondent the court may, on its own motion— (a) either— (i) in the case of an application to vary or revoke an interim order, make a new interim order for the former child protected person as a protected person if satisfied on the balance of probabilities— (A) that the former child protected person has been subjected to family violence committed by the respondent; and (B) that the interim order is necessary to protect the former child protected person pending a final decision about the application; or (ii) in the case of an application to vary or revoke a final order, make a new final order under section 74 or 76 for the former child protected person as a protected person; and (b) vary the order to which the application under section 100 relates as the court considers necessary. new: A person (A) commits an offence if— (a) A engages in a course of conduct in relation to another person (B); and (b) the course of conduct includes any conduct specified in subsection (2); and (c) either— (i) A intends that the course of conduct will cause a result described in subsection (3) or believes that the course of conduct will probably cause such a result; or (ii) A ought to understand, in all the particular circumstances, that the course of conduct will probably cause a result described in subsection (3) and the course of conduct does cause such a result. new: Division 3A—Interim orders made on court's own motion 43A Definitions for this Division In this Division— application or appeal relating to bail means any of the following under the Bail Act 1977— (a) an application for bail; (b) an application to vary conditions of bail; (c) an application to extend bail; (d) an application to revoke bail; (e) an appeal under section 18A; (f) an appeal under section 18AG; relevant offence means any of the following offences— (a) a sexual offence listed in clause 1 of Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 1991; (b) a violent offence listed in clause 2 of Schedule 1 to the Sentencing Act 1991; (c) an offence against section 21A of the Crimes Act 1958 (stalking); relevant party means, in a criminal proceeding, the party who— (a) is accused; or (b) has been found guilty; or (c) is appealing having been found guilty; or (d) has had their finding of guilt set aside on appeal. 43B Application of Division This Division does not apply to a relevant party who was a child at the time of the alleged commission of a relevant offence. 43C Court hearing application or appeal relating to bail may make own motion interim order (1) Subject to section 43E, a court hearing an application or appeal relating to bail in respect of a relevant offence may make an interim order against a relevant party to protect an alleged victim of the relevant offence if the court is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that the interim order is necessary to ensure the safety of the alleged victim pending a decision about a final order. (2) A court may make an interim order under this section on its own motion. (3) Without limiting subsection (1), in deciding whether it is appropriate to make an interim order, the court may consider— (a) whether the relevant party has a cognitive impairment; and (b) if the court is satisfied the relevant party has a cognitive impairment, the relevant party's ability to do the following— (i) understand the nature and effect of an interim order; (ii) comply with the conditions of the interim order. (4) An interim order may be made under this section for more than one alleged victim of the relevant offence if the court is satisfied under subsection (1) in relation to each of the alleged victims. 43D Court may make interim order on its own motion in a criminal proceeding (1) Subject to section 43E, a court hearing a criminal proceeding for a relevant offence may make an interim order against a relevant party to protect an alleged victim of the relevant offence if the court is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that the interim order is necessary to ensure the safety of the alleged victim pending a decision about a final order. (2) A court may make an interim order under this section on its own motion. (3) Without limiting subsection (1), in deciding whether it is appropriate to make an interim order, the court may consider— (a) whether the relevant party has a cognitive impairment; and (b) if the court is satisfied the relevant party has a cognitive impairment, the relevant party's ability to do the following— (i) understand the nature and effect of an interim order; (ii) comply with the conditions of the interim order. (4) The court may make an interim order under subsection (1)— (a) at any stage of the criminal proceeding, including during any committal hearing, any trial, any sentencing hearing or any appeal; and (b) whether or not the person accused is found guilty of the offence; and (c) whether or not the charge is withdrawn or the prosecution of the offence is discontinued. (5) An interim order may be made under this section for more than one alleged victim if the court is satisfied under subsection (1) in relation to each of the alleged victims of the relevant offence. 43E Court must not make interim order in certain circumstances The court must not make an interim order under section 43C or 43D if— (a) the alleged victim is a family member of the relevant party; or (b) there is an existing personal safety intervention order that protects the alleged victim from the relevant party; or (c) an application for a personal safety intervention order that protects the alleged victim from the relevant party has been made but not finally determined. 43F Prosecutor not party to proceeding for interim order (1) The prosecutor in any criminal proceeding in which an interim order is made or proposed to be made under this Division is not a party to the proceeding, and has no standing or status in the proceeding, only for the purposes of the making of the interim order. (2) Nothing in subsection (1) affects the status, function or standing of a prosecutor in relation to the criminal proceeding other than the making of the interim order. 43G Material before the court for making interim orders under this Division (1) Nothing in Division 4 applies to the making of an interim order under section 43C or 43D. (2) An interim order under section 43C or 43D must be made on the material before the court in the hearing of the application or appeal relating to bail, or the criminal proceeding. 43H Interim order to protect child if interim order made under section 43C or 43D (1) This section applies if— (a) the court makes an interim order under section 43C or 43D; and (b) the court is satisfied, on the balance of probabilities, that a child who is a family member of the protected person has been subjected to prohibited behaviour committed by the relevant party. (2) Subject to subsection (3), if the court is satisfied that it is necessary to make an interim order to protect the child or ensure the safety of the child pending a decision about a final order, the court may— (a) if the child's need for protection is substantially the same as that of the person to be protected by the interim order, include the child in the interim order as a protected person; or (b) otherwise, make a separate interim order for the child as a protected person. (3) The court must not make an interim order for the child if— (a) the child is a family member of the relevant party; or (b) there is an existing personal safety intervention order that protects the child from the relevant party; or (c) an application for a personal safety intervention order that protects the child from the relevant party has been made but not finally determined. 43I Oral explanation of interim order (1) If the court makes an interim order under this Division and the relevant party or the protected person or both are before the court, the court must give the relevant party and the protected person (as the case requires) a clear oral explanation of the matters referred to in section 40(1). (2) A failure by the court to give an oral explanation in accordance with this section does not affect the validity of the interim order. 43J Documents to be given to relevant party who is before the court If the court makes an interim order under this Division, and the relevant party is before the court, the court must give the relevant party— (a) a copy of the interim order; and (b) a brief written statement of the reasons for making the interim order; and (c) a written notice of the matters referred to in section 40(1) in the form prescribed by the rules of the court making the interim order. 43K Service of interim order and other documents If the court makes an interim order under this Division— (a) the appropriate registrar for the court must arrange for the relevant party who is not before the court to be served with— (i) a copy of the interim order; and (ii) a brief written statement of the reasons for making the interim order; and (iii) a written notice of the matters referred to in section 40(1) in the form prescribed by the rules of the court making the interim order; and (b) the appropriate registrar for the court must arrange for the protected person to be served with— (i) a copy of the interim order; and (ii) a brief written statement of the reasons for making the interim order; and (iii) a written notice of the matters referred to in section 40(1) in the form prescribed by the rules of the court making the interim order. 43L Interim order taken to be application for personal safety intervention order and treated as application under this Act If an interim order is made under section 43C or 43D, for the purposes of this Act— (a) the interim order is taken to be— (i) an application for a personal safety intervention order; and (ii) a summons for the relevant party to attend the relevant court at the first mention date stated in the order for the application for a personal safety intervention order; and (b) the Chief Commissioner of Police is taken to be the applicant in relation to the application; and (c) any interim order made under section 43H(2)(b) is taken to form part of the application referred to in paragraph (a); and (d) an application for a personal safety intervention order referred to in paragraph (a) may be withdrawn or otherwise dealt with as an application in accordance with this Act. 43M Interim orders made by Supreme or County Court to be transferred to Magistrates' Court for final determination (1) If an interim order is made by the Supreme Court or the County Court under section 43C or 43D the proceeding for the final order is transferred to the Magistrates' Court for determination. (2) On an application under Division 10, the Magistrates' Court may revoke or vary the interim order as if the order had been made by that court. 43N Mention date and hearing for proceeding for final order If an interim order is made by a court under this Division, the Magistrates' Court must ensure that— (a) the proceeding for the final order is listed for mention— (i) if the relevant party was before the court when the interim order was made, within 14 days of the making of the order; or (ii) otherwise, within 14 days of the interim order being served on the relevant party; and (b) the hearing to determine the final order is listed as soon as practicable.
